top.title: Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO
top.description: The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has restored all transmission lines that tripped during a grid disturbance on Friday. The management of NISO said this in a statement in Abuja on Friday. The ​‌‍‌​⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠​⁠​​‌‍‌​system operator also said that the incident was not a system collapse. It said that the disturbance resulted from the tripping of some transmission line, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”NISO wishes to clarify that the grid disturbance experienced earlier today was not a system collapse. “It resulted from the tripping of some transmission lines, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”At 12:34 p.m., the Omotosho–Ikeja West transmission line tripped, resulting in a significant load drop within the Lagos Complex. ”Subsequently, at 12:50 p.m, the Ihovbor–Oshogbo transmission line tripped alongside the Benin–Egbin and Ihovbor–Ajaokuta transmission lines, resulting in load losses in some parts of the country,” it said. The system operator said that prompt emergency response measures were activated by the relevant operational teams in coordination with TCN to stabilize the grid and restore affected transmission lines. It said that all the affected lines had since been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49 p.m. on Friday. It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, coordinating system operations, and ensuring the reliable and secure operation of the Nigerian electricity grid. ”The public is advised to rely on official communications from NISO for accurate information on developments within the national electricity grid,” it said. top.title: SB Nation Reacts: Arizona football fans pick their preferred bowl slot
top.description: San Diego, California - January 02: Arizona and SMU players run over the Holiday Bowl logo during the Holiday Bowl at Snapdragon Stadium on Friday, Jan. 2, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images) Arizona will be playing in a bowl game next month, marking the first time since 2012-15 it gets to go bowling in consecutive season. The Wildcats have been bowl eligible in three of the last four years. But which bowl game will the UA play in? Despite being in the Big 12 Conference since 2014, Arizona is still considered a so-called “Pac-12 legacy school” when it comes to bowl affiliations. This is the last year of this connection, meaning after the 2027 season the Wildcats will be able to play in a whole different set of bowls (assuming they’re still around with the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams). We asked our readers which of the most likely bowl destinations they think Arizona will end up, and a plurality are expecting a repeat of last season. Arizona lost 24-19 to SMU at the Holiday Bowl in January, a game it trailed 24-0 before making a late push for the comeback. It was the UA’s first appearance in the San Diego-based game since 2009. Holiday is the third in the pecking order for bowl selections among Pac-12 legacy teams, with the Alamo Bowl getting first pick and then Las Vegas. The Sun Bowl is fourth, followed by the Poinsettia Bowl and Independence Bowl. Arizona beat Oklahoma in the 2023 Alamo Bowl but hasn’t been in the Vegas or Sun bowls in a long time. The last appearance in Sin City for a bowl game was in 2008, a 31-21 win over BYU, and the last trip to El Paso for the Sun Bowl resulted in a 20-15 loss to Baylor in 1992. Arizona is one of seven Pac-12 legacy schools that are currently bowl-eligible, while Oregon State and Stanford are each a win away from six. UCLA and Utah are virtual locks for the College Football Playoff, taking them out of the mix, while Oregon and USC could also sneak into the 12-team field. If not, those squads would be likely be the first choices for bowls ahead of Arizona.

top.title: 2026 D-backs Off-season questions, #3: Trading Ketel Marte, or not?
top.description: SAN DIEGO, CA - SEPTEMBER 25: Ketel Marte #4 of the Arizona Diamondbacks warms up during the game between the Arizona Diamondbacks and the San Diego Padres at Petco Park on Friday, September 25, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Brendon Baranov/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images In his final game of 2026, Ketel Marte passed Luis Gonzalez as the all-time Diamondbacks leader for games played, appearing in his 1,195th regular season contest for Arizona. He is now ranked top three in most offensive counting stats, alongside Gonzalez and Paul Goldschmidt. There are still four seasons left on the contract extension which Marte signed in April 2025. But there is a very real possibility that Ketel has played his final game for the D-backs. Indications are that the team is now looking to trade him, the second baseman having apparently worn out his welcome in Arizona, barely eighteen months after signing that six-year extension. We recently discussed the rumors about a potential Marte trade. At the time of writing, the Baltimore Orioles and the Toronto Blue Jays are the teams who have been most frequently mentioned as a landing spot in any trade. Though with his long-term status on the Diamondbacks, Ketel now has the full ability to decline any move, a situation which complicates the process considerably. But will the team pull the trigger? And should they, especially if the return is not one they consider appropriate for a player of Marte’s undeniable talents. We are, after all, barely a year removed from Ketel winning the Silver Slugger and being mentioned on MVP ballots. However, Mrs. SnakePit would likely point to Marte’s performance since the contract extension as further evidence for her theory that giving large, long-term contact extensions to players is frequently a mistake. top.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
top.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . It's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns

top.title: Florida State pulls away in second half to cruise past Green Bay
top.description: Nov 20, 2026; Tallahassee, Florida, USA; Florida State Seminoles forward Shon Abaev (1) dribbles the ball during the second half against the Green Bay Phoenix at Donald L. Tucker Center. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida State overcame a choppy first half and a scrappy Green Bay team to pull away in the second half, cruising to an 87-63 home win behind strong nights from Shon Abaev (a career-high 24 points) and Sebastian Rancik (24 points, one off his career high set in the Florida A&M season-opener). First Half Florida State won the tip, and immediately Abaev drilled a clean three to open the game, but Green Bay answered right back. Fifth-year guard Orlando Lovejoy scored a couple of layups to keep the Phoenix within striking distance early. Abaev answered with another triple, then the Noles got out in transition with a Kam Taylor layup on the break, and Alex Steen followed with a dunk that got the crowd back into it. Anthony Robinson II was back after dealing with a nagging foot injury, and the difference was obvious. The offense looked sharper with him on the floor. He brought the energy and direction that was missing against Ball State. Florida State led 11-10 with 15:19 left at the first media timeout. Martay Barnes and Elisee Assui checked in, but the Noles stayed stuck in an offensive slump and couldn’t string together stops. Green Bay went 5-for-6 over the next stretch heading into the second media timeout. Marcis Ponder struggled to find any rhythm early. "What they (selectors and team management) are doing with him is not right. They are not encouraging him; they are discouraging him, which is not done. These guys are making a blunder. top.title: ‘He’s done’ – Stephen A. Smith says there is no way back for Dallas Cowboys man who he simply cannot defend
top.description: Photo by Ben Liebenberg/Getty Images Stephen A. Smith says there is no way back for Christian Parker with the Dallas Cowboys even if they do improve. Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker has been stripped of his responsibility to call plays. The decision was made earlier in the week after the team’s 46-40 loss at home to the San Francisco 49ers. The Cowboys gave up almost 600 yards, with their defense now ranking dead last after 10 games. Parker’s responsibilities will be taken on by Mike Pettine, who was originally brought in as a consultant to help him out. Speaking to First Take, Stephen A. What if Mike Pettine does right this ship? What if the Dallas Cowboys elevate to decent or respectable? What if that happens? “Well, then Christian Parker isn’t going to get his job back. “It’s not like you’re going to turn around and say, ‘OK, you can come back now that somebody else has corrected it.’ You aren’t going to do that. “So clearly, the bottom line is he’s done, any way you want to slice it.” Stephen A. Now you’re going to be one to Mike Pettine? “I’m sorry, that’s a downgrade as far as I’m concerned.” Smith adds that while Parker cannot be defended, he believes the players must take their share of the blame. “I just needed to take a moment to point the finger at the players. top.title: Cadillac Cancels Plan To Build Its Own V6 F1 Engine
top.description: General Motors is pumping the brakes on its Formula 1 engine timeline. Cadillac will push back the debut of its in-house F1 power unit by one full year, shifting from 2029 to 2030 so its factory engine program launches alongside Formula 1's newly proposed V8 regulations. Rather than dumping millions of dollars into building a complex V6 hybrid for a single lame-duck season, the American team will extend its customer engine partnership with Ferrari through the end of 2029. Originally, GM planned to transition Cadillac from a Ferrari customer outfit into a full-fledged works team in 2029, operating under the assumption that the current 1.6-liter V6 hybrid cycle would run through 2030 before new rules arrived in 2031. Related Video That timeline accelerated ahead of this week's Las Vegas Grand Prix. Formula 1, the FIA, and existing engine manufacturers reached an agreement in principle to cut the current engine cycle short and introduce the 2.1-liter turbocharged V8s with scaled-back hybrid assistance starting in 2030. The paperwork still awaits final sign-off from the FIA World Motor Sport Council next month, McLaren CEO Zak Brown confirmed it was happening during Thursday's team principals' press conference. "Yes, we would remain a customer of Ferrari through 2029 and bring the Cadillac power unit online in 2030 with the V8," Cadillac F1 CEO Dan Towriss told Motorsport.com in Las Vegas. "I think we're glad to see the series really coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030," Towriss said. "We're super happy with that." Why not? General Motors has a rich history of building race-winning V8 engines, from muscle cars to sports cars to IndyCars. Work back in the States is ramping up fast. General Motors will officially open its dedicated F1 power unit headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, on December 18. Once the doors open, engineers will temporarily run parallel development programs-using their existing V6 groundwork as a baseline while pivoting primary design efforts toward the 2030 V8. "Well, for a period of time, we're working on both," Towriss explained. "So they've already got a V6 base to build off of and then we're working towards the V8. There are a number of designs that are in motion now, so there's a lot of good foundation for what we're trying to build and the direction we're headed in." Of course, there are questions about the team's future after news broke that Mark Walter is reportedly exploring a sale of TWG's stake in Cadillac Formula 1 amid the ongoing DOJ and SEC investigation into the holding company. With an asking price of no less than $3 billion, there are rumored to be at least seven interested parties. Will Cadillac F1 survive until GM's engine is ready? Become an AutoGuide insider. Commending the unions for organising the conference to educate their members, the monarch said an informed labour union was essential to the survival of democracy and the development of the nation. He said stakeholders must work together to restore the country’s textile industry, revive moribund mills and make locally manufactured fabrics a source of national pride. “It is important for stakeholders to protect our industry. Let us prioritise our own fabrics. Let us revive our textile mills. Let us make Made in Nigeria a badge of pride, not an apology. “We must honour labour. nigeria.title: 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa
nigeria.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary election of the party, was unlawfully substituted by Ribadu. Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary. However, he was later replaced by Ribadu. Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution. He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party. He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party. Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died. He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void. The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. nigeria.description: Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function. The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers. How SHRINCS works SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both. Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block. The risk of a stateful signature The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size. Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.” Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. A song should not earn a nomination simply because it is popular or has enjoyed international success. sports.title: SB Nation Reacts: Arizona football fans pick their preferred bowl slot
sports.description: San Diego, California - January 02: Arizona and SMU players run over the Holiday Bowl logo during the Holiday Bowl at Snapdragon Stadium on Friday, Jan. 2, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images) Arizona will be playing in a bowl game next month, marking the first time since 2012-15 it gets to go bowling in consecutive season. The Wildcats have been bowl eligible in three of the last four years. But which bowl game will the UA play in? Despite being in the Big 12 Conference since 2014, Arizona is still considered a so-called “Pac-12 legacy school” when it comes to bowl affiliations. This is the last year of this connection, meaning after the 2027 season the Wildcats will be able to play in a whole different set of bowls (assuming they’re still around with the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams). We asked our readers which of the most likely bowl destinations they think Arizona will end up, and a plurality are expecting a repeat of last season. Arizona lost 24-19 to SMU at the Holiday Bowl in January, a game it trailed 24-0 before making a late push for the comeback. It was the UA’s first appearance in the San Diego-based game since 2009. Holiday is the third in the pecking order for bowl selections among Pac-12 legacy teams, with the Alamo Bowl getting first pick and then Las Vegas. The Sun Bowl is fourth, followed by the Poinsettia Bowl and Independence Bowl. Arizona beat Oklahoma in the 2023 Alamo Bowl but hasn’t been in the Vegas or Sun bowls in a long time. The last appearance in Sin City for a bowl game was in 2008, a 31-21 win over BYU, and the last trip to El Paso for the Sun Bowl resulted in a 20-15 loss to Baylor in 1992. Arizona is one of seven Pac-12 legacy schools that are currently bowl-eligible, while Oregon State and Stanford are each a win away from six. UCLA and Utah are virtual locks for the College Football Playoff, taking them out of the mix, while Oregon and USC could also sneak into the 12-team field. If not, those squads would be likely be the first choices for bowls ahead of Arizona.

We recently discussed the rumors about a potential Marte trade. At the time of writing, the Baltimore Orioles and the Toronto Blue Jays are the teams who have been most frequently mentioned as a landing spot in any trade. Though with his long-term status on the Diamondbacks, Ketel now has the full ability to decline any move, a situation which complicates the process considerably. But will the team pull the trigger? Srikkanth believes the 15-year-old has the potential to become a match-winner across formats and even play a significant role in reviving Test cricket globally. Speaking at the sports event on Friday, Srikkanth said the selectors and team management were making a mistake by not providing Sooryavanshi with enough opportunities. 'They are discouraging him': Srikkanth slams selectors over Sooryavanshi's treatment Srikkanth questioned the decision to pick Sooryavanshi for one match and then leave him out for several games, stressing that the youngster needed sustained opportunities to prove his abilities. "What they (selectors and team management) are doing with him is not right. They are not encouraging him; they are discouraging him, which is not done. These guys are making a blunder. They play him for one match, they don't play him for five matches. That's not done. Sad," Srikkanth said at the event. 'Test cricket revival happens all over the world': Srikkanth backs Sooryavanshi's potential Going a step further, Srikkanth suggested that Sooryavanshi's success in the longest format could generate renewed interest in Test cricket, not just in India but across the cricketing world. The decision was made earlier in the week after the team’s 46-40 loss at home to the San Francisco 49ers. The Cowboys gave up almost 600 yards, with their defense now ranking dead last after 10 games. And I don’t think Mike Pettine is going to do a damn thing, personally, if they go ahead and make this change. “Well, my point is, let’s take the opposite approach, let’s take the Skip Bayless approach. What if Mike Pettine does right this ship? What if the Dallas Cowboys elevate to decent or respectable? What if that happens? “Well, then Christian Parker isn’t going to get his job back. “It’s not like you’re going to turn around and say, ‘OK, you can come back now that somebody else has corrected it.’ You aren’t going to do that. “So clearly, the bottom line is he’s done, any way you want to slice it.” Stephen A. Smith says Parker is now worse off The Cowboys hired Christian Parker after his two-year stint as the passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach on the Philadelphia Eagles. Smith argues that he is now in a worse position after his setback with the Cowboys: “He was an assistant to Vic Fangio in Philadelphia, a disciple of his. Now you’re going to be one to Mike Pettine? “I’m sorry, that’s a downgrade as far as I’m concerned.” Smith adds that while Parker cannot be defended, he believes the players must take their share of the blame. “I just needed to take a moment to point the finger at the players. sports.title: Cadillac Cancels Plan To Build Its Own V6 F1 Engine
sports.description: General Motors is pumping the brakes on its Formula 1 engine timeline. Cadillac will push back the debut of its in-house F1 power unit by one full year, shifting from 2029 to 2030 so its factory engine program launches alongside Formula 1's newly proposed V8 regulations. Rather than dumping millions of dollars into building a complex V6 hybrid for a single lame-duck season, the American team will extend its customer engine partnership with Ferrari through the end of 2029. Originally, GM planned to transition Cadillac from a Ferrari customer outfit into a full-fledged works team in 2029, operating under the assumption that the current 1.6-liter V6 hybrid cycle would run through 2030 before new rules arrived in 2031. Related Video That timeline accelerated ahead of this week's Las Vegas Grand Prix. Formula 1, the FIA, and existing engine manufacturers reached an agreement in principle to cut the current engine cycle short and introduce the 2.1-liter turbocharged V8s with scaled-back hybrid assistance starting in 2030. The paperwork still awaits final sign-off from the FIA World Motor Sport Council next month, McLaren CEO Zak Brown confirmed it was happening during Thursday's team principals' press conference. "Yes, we would remain a customer of Ferrari through 2029 and bring the Cadillac power unit online in 2030 with the V8," Cadillac F1 CEO Dan Towriss told Motorsport.com in Las Vegas. "I think we're glad to see the series really coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030," Towriss said. "We're super happy with that." Why not? General Motors has a rich history of building race-winning V8 engines, from muscle cars to sports cars to IndyCars. Work back in the States is ramping up fast. General Motors will officially open its dedicated F1 power unit headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, on December 18. Once the doors open, engineers will temporarily run parallel development programs-using their existing V6 groundwork as a baseline while pivoting primary design efforts toward the 2030 V8. "Well, for a period of time, we're working on both," Towriss explained. "So they've already got a V6 base to build off of and then we're working towards the V8. There are a number of designs that are in motion now, so there's a lot of good foundation for what we're trying to build and the direction we're headed in." Of course, there are questions about the team's future after news broke that Mark Walter is reportedly exploring a sale of TWG's stake in Cadillac Formula 1 amid the ongoing DOJ and SEC investigation into the holding company. With an asking price of no less than $3 billion, there are rumored to be at least seven interested parties. Will Cadillac F1 survive until GM's engine is ready? Become an AutoGuide insider. sports.title: Formula 1’s Obsession With Spectacle Always Led It To Las Vegas
sports.description: F1 always intended to host a Grand Prix on the Las Vegas Strip, but it wouldn't come to fruition until 2023. (Photo credit: Mark Thompson, Getty Images/Red Bull Content Pool) Formula 1 has always had an appetite for spectacle. The Las Vegas Grand Prix has perfectly embodied that vision, as its earlier iteration, the Caesars Palace Grand Prix , remains a painful reminder of its pitfalls. Together they have marked important turning points for the future of the championship. Caesars Palace Grand Prix: F1's first foray into spectacle The Caesars Palace Grand Prix circuit was a relatively featureless track built in a casino parking lot. (Photo: Yoyodu10 via Wikimedia Commons) The first three decades of Formula 1 looked dramatically different from the sport we know today, in large part because it remained a fairly amateur affair. Grands Prix taking place in major city centers used to be a rarity. For the United States, that was evident when the sport came to compete at Watkins Glen International. Located in a sleepy hamlet in upstate New York, Watkins Glen was F1's first true American home, hosting the United States Grand Prix from 1961 to 1980. The track is nowhere near any major hub for air or sea travel, the town of Watkins Glen itself has rarely boasted more than 3,000 inhabitants since its founding in 1870, and the lodgings were as equally rudimentary as the track facilities. For a sport that in the 1960s was used to racing in the countryside of England, Belgium, and France, and that often failed to pay all but the top drivers a living wage, Watkins Glen was perfectly aligned with F1’s spirit. But the sport began to evolve in the 1970s. Advancements in technology resulted in quicker cars, while behind-the-scenes politics brought about an increase in prize purses and the introduction of television broadcast package sales. F1 thus began to reach wider audiences, and the men in charge of the sport wanted to present Formula 1 as the pinnacle of motor racing in every aspect. That meant transforming the calendar. In 1976, Formula 1 added a new race in Long Beach, California. Organizer Chris Pook felt he had an opportunity to tie the international glamour of F1 to the glamour of nearby Los Angeles in order to create an unforgettable event. And it worked: the race, called the United States Grand Prix West, attracted plenty of celebrity attention, and drivers enjoyed the technical circuit. Pook had shown The Powers That Be in Formula 1 that a street circuit in an eye-catching location could work. So, F1 turned its eyes to Las Vegas. The 1970s was a decade of transition for Formula 1, and the city of Las Vegas. Construction had slowed after much of the mafia money funding casinos had been ousted, but visitor numbers nevertheless almost doubled. Boxing had long been a favored Vegas spectacle, but when daredevil Evel Knievel was contracted to jump over the fountains in front of Caesars Palace in 1967, motorsport entered the conversation. technology.title: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.
technology.description: The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons. Wireless industry lobby group CTIA said a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls. CTIA told the FCC in an October 1 filing : The pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate. Even with these constraints, the micro-jamming system blocked 911 calls, interfered with public safety and other communications, and caused interference that impacted wireless network infrastructure up to two and a half miles away. At the same time, the pilot results show substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts. CTIA said the pilot test shows "that current jamming technology seems to be both over and underinclusive at once—it risks blocking lawful communications even as it fails to block a significant portion of the targeted contraband device communications." technology.title: Nvidia’s journey to forge the one CPU SKU to rule them all
technology.description: Each generation of Intel Xeons or AMD Epycs brings dozens of new SKUs: high-core count parts tuned for throughput, high-frequency ones optimized for latency, low-power chips designed for the edge, and everything in between. But if you ask Ian Finder, who heads development of Nvidia’s datacenter CPUs, for the vast majority of use cases, all those SKUs are overkill. “There was sort of an overskewing, for many years on the other vendors side of things,” he told El Reg on the sidelines of Supercomputing 2026 this week. Nvidia is a relative newcomer to the datacenter CPU space. The company’s first part, called Grace, launched in 2023, but didn’t see widespread deployment outside AI headnodes, high-end NICs, and a handful of standalone CPU deployments by hyperscalers like Meta. We explored the chip in greater detail earlier this year, but the GPU slinger’s latest CPU, Vera, is a different beast. In addition to showing up as part of Nvidia’s Vera-Rubin superchips, the CPU will also be offered in standalone CPU racks, storage, and context memory systems. Just this week, Nvidia announced a new rack with 192 Vera CPUs aimed at high-performance computing (HPC) workloads, which don’t translate well to GPUs. And at least on paper, a single SKU with 88 cores clocking to 3.3 GHz powers all of them. Historically, CPUs with different combinations of cores, clocks, I/O, and power have been used in these roles. According to Finder, most datacenter CPUs haven’t been loaded that heavily, and as a result unloaded latency has been the optimization point. As a consequence, CPUs that rely on high core counts to boost throughput often suffer from elevated loaded latencies. On the flip side, chipmakers can optimize for loaded latency, but this usually comes at the expense of throughput. We see this pretty clearly across AMD’s last few generations of Epycs, where it designed both space-efficient Zen-C cores that prioritize throughput and fatter frequency-optimized versions that prioritize latency. “As more cores are up and running, your latency to memory gets higher because you have to deal with congestion on the connectivity buses,” More than Moore analyst Ian Cutress tells The Reg . “What Nvidia is saying is right. Sometimes, you do have to pick between core count and core latency.” A balanced architecture With Vera, Nvidia sought to thread that needle to design a balanced architecture that maintains low latencies and high throughput even when all 88 cores are loaded. This does mean making some compromises – in particular, the CPU's vector unit isn’t the beefiest. But if you’ve got GPUs capable of running vectorized code, that compromise starts to make a lot more sense – and if you’re buying Vera you almost certainly do. “If you do a few things like that, you can actually get a part that, for the workloads people care about — knowledge agents for CI/CD, for software engineering, or databases and analytics — you can build a part that gets you the same performance per core

The China-linked attacker used Cairn, an open source, penetration-testing framework that has become increasingly popular with cybercriminals who use the AI tool to carry out multi-stage intrusions with no human assistance . In this case, the agents found and exploited a zero-day MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging AI application. Amazon notified the project's maintainers of the vulnerability, and they released a fix and a security advisory . On September 10, Amazon's Threat Intelligence Team found a server with a publicly hosted instance of Cairn that provided visibility into the campaign targeting universities in East Asia, outside Mainland China, Moses said in a Friday report shared with The Register . The campaign occurred over a period of 48 hours beginning on September 8, and the prompts were written in Simplified Chinese, with timestamps in executed scripts configured to China Standard Time. Before the AI agents found and exploited the zero day, however, they tried to break into another university’s Redis server over about 16 hours and 148 sequential actions, including abusing Redis's replication feature to load unauthorized code, escaping its scripting sandbox, writing to its configuration files, and corrupting its memory. Meanwhile, a separate operation running for more than 6 hours targeted a university GPU server with another credential-spray attack, compiling a list of 80 real user names found across the school’s public websites, academic papers and other documents. The warning issued this week follows the regulator's previous work on smart glasses. The same warning mentioned the potential risks regarding data processing under the GDPR, as well as those related to the training of AI. technology.title: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
technology.description: The electronics industry faces a printed circuit board (PCB) shortage that could rival the pandemic-era chip crunch – with AI once again accused of hogging supplies. The Global Electronics Association says demand is arriving "at a scale the supply chain was not built for," straining everything from glass fabric and resin to finished boards. Its report, " The PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics ," says AI servers need increasingly complex boards. While a typical PC board has about 12 layers of tracks, AI server boards can have 40 to 60 layers or more, and each additional layer requires more resin, copper foil, and laminate. The supply of materials is set to be constrained through at least the first half of 2027, the report says, with meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. Programs to deliver PCBs for automotive, industrial, medical and even the defense industries are being crowded out as AI soaks up scarce capacity, it claims. The association's North American figures show orders growing much faster than deliveries. PCB bookings rose 56.1 percent in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, while PCB shipments increased 13.3 percent. Fabrication capacity is expanding, aimed at meeting the increased demand from the AI infrastructure sector, especially in Asia, where more than 90 percent of the world's boards are made. The report says that $10 billion has gone toward new PCB plants in Southeast Asia, and at least as much has been invested in China over the past three years, but the raw materials are themselves constrained. It warns of lengthening lead times for those raw materials. Standard FR-4 laminate now takes six to eight weeks to ship, up from two to three weeks a year ago, while advanced low-loss laminates now take 14 to 18 weeks for delivery, for example. Tightening supplies usually lead to price increases, and the report says that suppliers raised laminate costs by 30 percent in September, and that the price tag of some types of E-glass cloth for circuit boards has risen by 300 percent. The report also puts copper prices up 37 percent over the past year. Concerns have been raised about copper supplies before, as The Register has reported multiple times. The association compares the risk with the 2021 chip shortage , when disrupted supplies left manufacturers unable to secure even relatively mundane components. New capacity is coming, but it is late and comes in dribs and drabs, according to the report, while AI demand just keeps on absorbing it as soon as it arrives. The association's advice is for buyers to plan early, and to share realistic forecasts with suppliers rather than double-booking. Board makers should qualify alternative suppliers of materials such as laminate and copper foil before shortages bite, but it warns against stockpiling beyond real need, which adds to forward-buying pressure. But it would like governments to step in, of course, by tracking board and material lead times

science.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
science.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . It's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns

science.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
science.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . science.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
science.description: null For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth. Aldebaran is about 65 light-years away, while the Hyades are roughly 150 light-years distant. The orange eye of Taurus is a foreground star that happens to lie almost exactly along our line of sight toward the Hyades. This fact exposes one of the most convincing tricks in stargazing. The night sky looks flat, and our brains are extremely willing to believe it. But it has incredible depth — and when you can see parts of the night sky in 3D, that's when you begin to appreciate that you're not looking at a flat map. Instead, you begin to see our cosmic neighborhood as it really is. By appreciating depth, you learn its geography. What's happening and when to look Aldebaran, the brightest star in the constellation of Taurus. (Image credit: Christophe Lehenaff via Getty Images) Taurus is now easy to find from the Northern Hemisphere during the evening. Once it's dark, look east for a small, tight knot of stars — the Pleiades open cluster (M45) — and then look nearby for a much larger V-shaped arrangement. That V is the Hyades, with unmistakably orange Aldebaran apparently sitting on one arm. Aldebaran's name is derived from the Arabic Al Dabarān, meaning "the follower," because it appears to trail the Pleiades across the night sky. The Hyades is a real physical group of stars — an open cluster — that formed together and moves through our galaxy together. About 153 light-years away, the Hyades is the nearest open star cluster to Earth. The name means "the rainmakers" because their rising and setting times in the ancient Greek sky coincided with wet weather. Orange-red star Aldebaran — the 14th-brightest star in the night sky — is the interloper, sitting less than half as far away from the sun . science.description: null The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt. A t otal solar eclipse will sweep across the country , passing directly over Luxor and plunging some of ancient Egypt's greatest surviving monuments into darkness. Totality will begin in Luxor at approximately 1:02 p.m. EEST and last 6 minutes 22 seconds, according to Time and Date . We know when it will happen because we can calculate the motions of Earth and the moon centuries in advance. But run the same celestial clock backward and eclipses become one of nature's most precise timestamps. Astronomers can reconstruct where the moon's shadow fell thousands of years ago, even when nobody left a record of it. When an ancient text reliably describes an eclipse, it can anchor a moment in history to a specific place and time. Did an eclipse rewrite the Pyramid Age? Pharaoh Shepseskaf's huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara (Image credit: Jon Bodsworth - www.egyptarchive.co.uk) We know from astronomical calculations that eclipses crossed Egypt long before anyone left an identifiable written record of one. On April 1, 2471 B.C., a total solar eclipse swept across northern Egypt during the age of the great pyramid builders. In research published in 2025, archaeoastronomer Giulio Magli at the Polytechnic University of Milan proposed that the eclipse may help explain why Pharaoh Shepseskaf broke with tradition and built a huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara instead of a pyramid. It's a tantalizing hypothesis, but no surviving Egyptian text records the eclipse. Astronomers can calculate that an eclipse happened, but using it as a historical timestamp requires evidence that someone actually saw it and recorded it. science.description: null Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought. Up-front finding The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits." Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations. The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites , which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security." While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests. There are a range of threats to space-based services, both commercial and military. Some are reversible, while others are not. (Image credit: DIA) Counterspace worries A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system. Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report: Antisatellite (ASAT) missiles are designed to kinetically strike and destroy satellites. ASAT missiles could produce massive amounts of debris that can remain in orbit for decades or even centuries. The question is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, which will award a $1 million prize for an accepted solution. science.title: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured
science.description: null An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity. That, in turn, verifies Einstein's greatest theory, general relativity , which first predicted the existence of black holes and what their immediate surroundings would look like. Captured by a global network of telescopes forming an interferometer called the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and revealed to the public in 2019, the image shows the supermassive black hole at the heart of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87), located 55 million light-years away. The image of this black hole , designated M87*, with a mass around 6.5 billion times that of the sun, was an immense scientific achievement. That may lead to the question: why did it need verifying at all? Team leader and researcher with Australia's Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), Samuel Lai explained why capturing the image of a distant black hole is so tricky. "It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the moon," Lai said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. Lai and his small Australian team developed advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to capture information about the black hole's structure and filter out interference resulting from the fact that the EHT was viewing M87* from within our planet's atmosphere. The machine-learning technique called GenDIReCT also accounted for biases introduced by combining telescopes to create an Earth-sized interferometer. "When we applied it to the original EHT dataset, we found a black hole almost identical in size and shape as the historic EHT image. Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data," Lai continued. "This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process." This could settle the questions of just how the final image of M87* was influenced by both atmospheric effects and the processing methods needed to reconstruct pictures from telescope data. General relativity suggested that objects with mass curve the very fabric of space and time, united as a single entity called spacetime. Gravity arises from that curvature. The greater the mass, the more extreme the curvature and thus the greater the gravitational influence of that object. Taking this to its extreme, scientist Karl Schwarzschild came up with a solution to the equations of general relativity that suggested an infinitesimal region with infinite mass, resulting in unrestrained curvature, a singularity. The robotic Dragon capsule undocked from the International Space Station (ISS) today at 12:05 p.m. EST (1705 GMT), while the duo were flying 260 miles (418 kilometers) above western China. If all goes according to plan, the freighter will splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov. 21) at about 4:55 p.m. EST (2155 GMT). There will be no livestream for its reentry and splashdown. (Today's departure webcast did not feature live footage of the moment of undocking, as it occurred during a gap in coverage of the high-bandwidth signal needed for video.) The Dragon launched Oct. 13, on a mission called CRS-35 because it's the 35th that SpaceX has flown for NASA's Commercial Resupply Services program. The capsule arrived at the ISS on Oct. 15 , delivering more than 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of food, scientific gear and other supplies to the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. It will bring a lot of stuff down to Earth, too. "Thousands of pounds of cargo are returning from the space station, including research samples that could advance future space exploration and improve life on Earth," NASA officials wrote in an update on Tuesday (Nov. 17). "The returning research includes a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct scientists used to study vascular aging and cardiovascular disease in space and on Earth ," they added. Dragon is the only cargo craft flying today that's capable of making such downward deliveries. The others — Northrop Grumman's Cygnus, Russia's Progress vehicle and Japan's HTV-X — are all expendable and burn up in Earth's atmosphere to wrap up their first and only spaceflight. science.title: The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury
science.description: Artist’s impression of BepiColombo orbiting Mercury ESA/ATG medialab After a long and ponderous journey, the BepiColombo spacecraft will finally enter Mercury’s orbit on 21 November. Over the course of the next year, it will investigate the planet’s geology, its tenuous atmosphere and its magnetic field in an effort to understand how it formed and evolved over time. BepiColombo , a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), launched in October 2018. Mercury’s proximity to the sun makes it incredibly difficult to reach without overshooting the planet and falling into the sun, so the spacecraft had to take a long and looping path over the past eight years, flying past both Venus and Mercury several times and using their gravity to make subtle tweaks to its trajectory. In 2024, an issue with the thrusters lengthened that journey even further, pushing the arrival date back from 2025 to 2026. Now, it has finally arrived. Read more 6 of the most fascinating moments in the life of our solar system While it is arriving at Mercury as a single spacecraft, BepiColombo actually comprises two separate orbiters: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO, or Mio). In December, the two will split apart and move to different orbits – MPO on a near-circular path that takes 2.3 hours to complete an orbit, and Mio on a more distant elliptical orbit, where it will take 9.3 hours to circle Mercury. Advertisement Those split orbits complement the differing scientific objectives of the two spacecraft. MPO is more than twice the size of MMO, and its 11 scientific instruments focus largely on studying Mercury itself . Its instruments include several types of spectrometer to measure the makeup of the surface, a laser altimeter to map its terrain and instruments to study the makeup of Mercury’s extremely thin atmosphere, called an exosphere. Mio’s more distant orbit will allow it to study a broader area around Mercury. It has five sets of scientific instruments to study the magnetic field and atmosphere of the planet, as well as the solar wind that blows strongly in the area close to the sun. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter Now that the BepiColombo spacecraft are entering orbit, their primary mission is expected to last only one Earth year, which is a little more than four Mercury years. The mission could potentially be extended for another year, but beyond that the combination of limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it all but impossible to keep going. Over the course of the year, researchers hope that BepiColombo will provide enough data to solve some of Mercury’s many mysteries. Mercury’s magnetic field is bewildering, because it originates 400 kilometres above the planet’s centre and should have faded away long ago. Its atmosphere must be continuously supplied with material from the surface, but we are unsure exactly how that occurs.

On November 15, 2026 , the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier , the system intensified rapidly , thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones . Xavier was the basin’s second named storm of the season, following only Wati , a short-lived storm that emerged in October. As Xavier developed, NASA satellite data showed the storm churning along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water spanning from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific—a telltale sign of the El Niño that has been present in the region since June . When the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured this image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026 (4:53 p.m. Cook Islands Time on November 16), forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour later that day, a Category 5 storm on the cyclone intensity scale used in the region or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale . The storm ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record, noted Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach . Xavier’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual, but its easterly position aligns with research that indicates that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Research also shows that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace . According to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. It then encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment and slowly weakened as it pushed westward, reducing the threat that it posed to Samoa and American Samoa. science.title: Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone
science.description: null PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth , something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary. Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2 , flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1 's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space. "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. What an incredible milestone," Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker said during Thursday's event. An unexpected, but manageable, anomaly While this day and this week have been chock-full of excitement over the distance milestone, the Voyager mission team has been hard at work, as usual, keeping the two nearly 50-year-old spacecraft alive and functioning. Unfortunately, as JPL spokesperson Raquel Villanueva shared at this celebration, on Saturday (Nov. 14), Voyager 1 stopped transmitting science and engineering data. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 while investigating the issue, and they are confident that they'll be able to solve it soon. NASA and Voyager team members celebrate Voyager 1's light-day milestone at NASA JPL on Nov. 19, 2026. From left to right: Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate; Jonathan Lunine, chief scientist, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory; Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager; Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager; Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd) "We listen to each spacecraft every day," Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd told Space.com at the event. Regarding Voyager 1, "we have an anomaly that is not something unseen before," Dodd said. "We do have a very strong carrier signal. We currently don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently." "But if you recall," Dodd added, "one light-day is very far from us. [It takes] 24 hours to get the signal to the spacecraft, 24 hours for the signal to come down, so it takes two days to diagnose anything on the spacecraft … So we can't do anything fast, and the data rates are very low."
